name: Cairngorms National Park
tagline: The UK's largest national park, a vast wilderness of ancient pine forest, ice-carved mountains and genuine Highland wildlife.

shortDescription: The UK's largest national park, a vast Highland wilderness of ancient Caledonian pine forest, ice-carved mountains and real wildlife around every glen.

intro: Cairngorms National Park is genuinely the UK's largest national park, a vast stretch of Highland wilderness considerably bigger than many small countries, built around a range of ancient, ice-carved mountains.

Its real character is genuinely in its scale and wildness — ancient Caledonian pine forest, some of Britain's last remaining fragments, shelters red deer, red squirrels and golden eagles across glens that feel largely untouched.

Most visitors genuinely base themselves in Aviemore, a small outdoor-focused town at the park's heart, using it as a launchpad for hiking, wildlife watching and, in winter, some of Scotland's only skiing.

whyVisit.intro: The Cairngorms' case rests on genuinely vast scale and real, accessible Highland wildlife.

points.title: It's genuinely the UK's largest national park
points.text: Bigger than Luxembourg, with a real sense of scale and wildness rare in Britain.

points.title: Ancient Caledonian pine forest survives genuinely here
points.text: Some of Scotland's last remaining fragments of its original native forest.

points.title: Wildlife spotting is genuinely a real possibility, not a gimmick
points.text: Red deer, red squirrels and golden eagles are all genuinely present across the park.

points.title: The Cairngorm Mountain Railway is genuinely accessible
points.text: A funicular climbing high into the mountains without requiring a serious hike.

points.title: It works genuinely well alongside Speyside and Loch Ness
points.text: A natural stop on a wider Highland loop, both within easy driving distance.

attractionsIntro: The park's essential sights combine ancient forest, genuine wildlife and some of Scotland's highest mountain terrain.

attractions.name: Loch Morlich

image.alt: Loch Morlich beneath the Cairngorm Mountains

attractions.text: Genuinely a striking freshwater loch backed directly by the Cairngorm mountains, with a sandy beach unusual for inland Scotland.
attractions.tip: Genuinely popular for watersports in summer, with rental kayaks and paddleboards available lakeside.

attractions.name: Aviemore

image.alt: The town of Aviemore in the Cairngorms

attractions.text: Genuinely the park's main town, a small, outdoor-focused hub of gear shops, cafés and easy access to the surrounding wilderness.
attractions.tip: Genuinely well stocked for last-minute hiking or ski gear before heading into the park.

attractions.name: The Cairngorm Mountain Railway
attractions.text: Genuinely the UK's highest railway, climbing to near the summit of Cairn Gorm without requiring a serious mountain hike.
attractions.tip: The genuinely summit can be significantly colder and windier than the base — dress accordingly.

attractions.name: Rothiemurchus Forest

image.alt: The ancient pine forest of Rothiemurchus

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Scotland's finest surviving fragments of ancient Caledonian pine forest, home to red squirrels and capercaillie.
attractions.tip: Genuinely well-marked trails suit every fitness level, from gentle loch walks to longer forest treks.

attractions.name: The park's red deer

image.file: File:Red Deer, River Muick, Cairngorms National Park, Scotland, Photo by Thomas Andy Branson.jpg
image.alt: A red deer in Cairngorms National Park

attractions.text: Genuinely a real, common sight across the park's glens, Britain's largest native land mammal in its natural Highland habitat.
attractions.tip: Genuinely dawn and dusk offer the best chances of a close, unhurried sighting.

attractions.name: The park's red squirrels

image.alt: A red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the park's most reliable wildlife sightings, native red squirrels thriving in the ancient pine forest.
attractions.tip: Genuinely feeding stations near Aviemore and Rothiemurchus offer near-guaranteed close sightings.

attractions.name: The Cairngorms' heather moorland

image.file: File:Common Heather, Cairngorms National Park, Scotland.jpg
image.alt: Heather moorland in Cairngorms National Park

attractions.text: Genuinely spectacular in late summer, when the park's open moorland turns a deep purple with flowering heather.
attractions.tip: Genuinely late August into September is peak bloom for the heather.

thingsToDoIntro: The park genuinely rewards slowing down, whether on foot, on the water or simply watching for wildlife.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the Cairngorm Mountain Railway

image.alt: The Cairngorm Mountain Railway climbing into the mountains

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely easy way to reach real mountain altitude, with sweeping views from the UK's highest railway.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check operating status ahead — the railway occasionally closes for maintenance or weather.

thingsToDo.title: Walk or paddle at Loch Morlich

image.alt: Sunset over Loch Morlich in the Cairngorms

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend an afternoon, whether walking the shoreline or paddling out onto the water.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely rent a kayak or paddleboard right at the loch for an hour or two on the water.

thingsToDo.title: Cycle or walk through Rothiemurchus Forest

image.file: File:Estate track in Rothiemurchus Forest - geograph.org.uk - 3619282.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely peaceful way to experience ancient Caledonian pine forest, with trails suited to every fitness level.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely bike rental is available right at the forest's visitor centre.

thingsToDo.title: Spot red squirrels and wildlife

image.alt: A red squirrel spotted in the Cairngorms

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding, patient activity, with real chances of red squirrels, deer and birds of prey across the park.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely bring binoculars — many of the park's best sightings reward a bit of patience and distance.

thingsToDo.title: Follow the Clunie Water on foot

image.file: File:Clunie Water, Cairngorms National Park, Scotland.jpg
image.alt: The Clunie Water flowing through Cairngorms National Park

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely gentle riverside walk, good for a shorter, easier day within the wider park.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with a picnic by the water on a fine day.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Aviemore's outdoor shops and cafés

image.alt: The main street of Aviemore in the Cairngorms

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely practical stop for last-minute gear, alongside a decent choice of cafés and restaurants.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a good spot to restock before or after a longer hike into the park.

gettingThere.intro: The Cairngorms are genuinely well connected by rail, sitting directly on Scotland's main Highland line.

options.text: Genuinely direct and scenic from both Glasgow and Inverness.
options.detail: One of Scotland's most useful rail links for reaching the Highlands without a car.

options.text: Genuinely useful for reaching the park's more remote glens and trailheads.
options.detail: About two and a half hours from Glasgow or Edinburgh.

options.text: Genuinely the closest airport, under an hour's drive from Aviemore.
options.detail: A practical option for visitors combining the park with Loch Ness or Skye.

gettingAround.intro: A car is genuinely the most flexible way to explore the park's spread-out trailheads and glens.

options.text: Genuinely essential for reaching the park's more remote hiking trailheads.
options.detail: Roads within the park are generally well maintained, if occasionally single-track.

options.mode: On foot or by bike in Aviemore
options.text: Genuinely easy — the town itself is small and walkable.
options.detail: Bike rental is widely available for reaching nearby Loch Morlich and Rothiemurchus.

options.text: Genuinely limited but useful for reaching some of the park's more popular sights without a car.
options.detail: Check current timetables, as rural Highland routes run less frequently than in cities.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for hiking, or winter for skiing
bestTime.summary: The Cairngorms are genuinely a year-round destination, offering hiking and wildlife in summer and Scotland's best skiing in winter.

seasons.text: Genuinely good hiking weather with fewer midges than midsummer.
The warmest season, with heather beginning to bloom by late summer, also genuinely peak midge season.
Genuinely excellent for wildlife, including the dramatic red deer rutting season.
Genuinely home to some of Scotland's only skiing, at the Cairngorm Mountain resort.

bestTime.avoid: Attempting higher mountain trails without proper gear in winter — genuinely serious alpine conditions above the tree line.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Cairngorms visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Check genuinely weather conditions before any higher-altitude hike — mountain weather shifts fast.
Pack genuinely proper layers and waterproofs regardless of season.
Book Cairngorm Mountain Railway tickets genuinely ahead in peak summer or ski season.
Bring genuinely midge repellent for summer visits, especially at dawn and dusk.
Rent bikes or watersports gear genuinely right at Loch Morlich or Rothiemurchus.
Allow genuinely extra time for wildlife spotting — patience matters more than covering ground quickly.

faq.q: How many days do you need in the Cairngorms?
faq.a: Two days genuinely covers Loch Morlich, the mountain railway and Rothiemurchus Forest comfortably.

faq.q: Is the Cairngorm Mountain Railway worth it?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's an easy way to reach real mountain altitude and views without a serious hike.

faq.q: Can you ski in the Cairngorms?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — the Cairngorm Mountain resort is one of Scotland's main ski areas, typically open December to March conditions permitting.

faq.q: What is Cairngorms National Park known for?
faq.a: Genuinely its vast scale, ancient Caledonian pine forest and real Highland wildlife, including red deer and red squirrels.

faq.q: Is the Cairngorms good for wildlife spotting?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely one of the best places in Britain, with real, reliable chances of red deer, red squirrels and birds of prey.

faq.q: Do you need a car in the Cairngorms?
faq.a: It genuinely helps for reaching remote trailheads, though Aviemore itself and nearby Loch Morlich are reachable without one.
